problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(0,1),(-1,2),(1,2).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation ${R}_{-\pi }$ by an angle of $\pi $ radians about the origin?

- $(1,1)$
- $(1,-2)$
- $(-1,3)$
worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-\pi }$ by an angle of $\pi $ radians is the same as counterclockwise rotation by the same angle. It's given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-\pi },$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-\pi }$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(0,-1),(1,-2),(-1,-2).$

So, the correct answer is "II only."
